intended_object: Right multiplication x ↦ x * g by a fixed element g, viewed as a smooth (C^∞) self-map of a manifold G whose multiplication is smooth (e.g. a Lie group). Inferred from the docstring, which says it mirrors the usual Lie group notation R_g.
explanation: The definition bundles the function `(· * g)` with its smoothness proof `contMDiff_mul_right`, giving an element of `C^∞⟮I, G; I, G⟯`. That is exactly the right-translation map R_g used in Lie theory. It asks for very little: only `Mul G`, a charted space structure on G and `ContMDiffMul I ∞ G`, i.e. that multiplication is smooth. It does not need a group or monoid structure, and the scalar field 𝕜 can be any nontrivially normed field. Choosing C^∞ instead of a general order n is deliberate, since the definition exists to provide the Lie group notation 𝑹. The definition is in Mathlib itself (`Mathlib/Geometry/Manifold/Algebra/Monoid.lean`), and Mathlib has no other declaration bundling this map, so there is no separate counterpart to cite. The definition is correct and at its natural generality.
